title: Requirement for Third Party Administrators to Adhere to Singapore Medical Council Ethical Guidelines
what_it_is: Requirement for Third Party Administrators to Adhere to Singapore Medical Council Ethical Guidelines

sections.label: MOH, TPA regulation, SMC guidelines
sections.summary: MOH lacks data on TPA-linked providers and does not regulate TPAs; SMC guidelines and powers cover doctors' fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) does not have the number of healthcare providers or doctors who have arrangements with TPAs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH does not regulate TPAs or their business arrangements today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Singapore Medical Council's (SMC's) Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG) provide guidance on appropriate fee arrangements between doctors and TPAs so as to ensure that patients' interest and welfare are protected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The SMC has statutory powers to take action against medical professionals who violate these guidelines.

sections.label: MOH monitoring TPA fee arrangements
sections.summary: MOH does not regulate TPAs not providing medical services, but monitors their fee arrangements and may consider further action.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Like I have mentioned before, MOH does not regulate TPAs who do not provide medical services directly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Those who do will be regulated under the Private Hospital Medical Clinics' Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: However, MOH acknowledges that the TPAs' fee arrangements may have an influence on the doctors' behaviour which can impact the charges and patient care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: While doctors are currently regulated by SMC to ensure that such TPA arrangements do not lead doctors to overcharge or compromise care, MOH will continue to monitor the situation and consider if further actions will be necessary to protect the well-being of the patients and also to prevent the escalation of healthcare costs.
